To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the tree representation of a graph naturally enables the message passing from the leaf nodes (neighbors of the root node) to the root node, and this message passing is demonstrated superior to the conventional ones in terms of performance and model scalability.

(1) the message passing scheme in the vanilla GCNs is suboptimal and the message passing scheme within the tree representation of graphs is superior; (2) the deep capability can be realized in the tree representation of graph neural networks.

the tree representation of graphs is a better representation than the graph representation, and that the upward message passing scheme is a superior message propagation scheme than the vanilla GCN and GAT's message passing schemes, and that the tree representation and the upward message passing can be combined into a deep architecture for graph learning.
